ety.text: From Middle English sculle, scolle (also schulle, scholle), probably from a dialectal form of Old Norse skalli (“bald head, skull”), itself probably related to Old English sċealu (“husk”), to Proto-Norse *ᛋᚲᚨᛚᛟ (*skalo), from Proto-Germanic *skallô; compare Finnish kallo. Compare Scots scull, Danish skal (“skull”) and skalle (“bald head, skull”), Norwegian skalle, Swedish skalle and especially dialectal Swedish skulle.

senses.d: The main bones of the head considered as a unit; including the cranium, facial bones, and mandible.
These bones as a symbol for death; death's-head.

ex: My thoughts are flying around in my skull like fireflies in a jar, but all of a sudden I'm unbearably tired and can't stay awake.

senses.d: A crust formed on the ladle, etc. by the partial cooling of molten metal.
The crown of the headpiece in armour.
The head or master of a college.
To hit in the head with a fist, a weapon, or a thrown object.
To strike the top of (the ball).
ex: Monte swung so hard at the next ball that he skulled it straight right, into the pond: 8 in, 9 out.

senses.d: To drink everything that remains in a glass by upending it.
ex: She nearly skulled the next drink and, despite feeling a little woozy, she felt a lot better.
He skulled his drink, set the glass down, then grabbed the bottle and ambled over to the other couch.
